newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close off highs on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close off highs on profit-taking.

text.p: French shares closed narrowly higher on Thursday as profit-taking ahead of Friday's monthly settlement knocked them from their best levels, dealers said.
Wall Street's sell-off also hit sentiment.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended 0.18 point or 0.01 percent higher at 2,233.57 while the CAC-40 futures contract settled 1.0 point lower at 2,238.0.
Volume was a heavy 6.1 billion francs.
Some analysts said the French market was starting to look fairly valued to expensive and that investors were scrambling for new reasons to buy.

In addition, some investors were starting to get fearful that Wall Street was ripe for a correction. "We've got to get increasingly cautious with New York," said one trader, attributing its gravity-defying performance of late to year-end "window dressing".

Club Mediterranee finished up 3.08 percent at 330.90 francs, adding to recent gains on market talk that leisure group Accor could launch a bid for the travel firm. Accor ended down 0.45 percent at 662 francs.

Moulinex jumped early in the day after companies controlled by Hungarian-born investor George Soros bought 5.5 percent of the troubled French appliance maker but then retraced much of its gains to close up 1.26 percent at 112.50 francs. Appliance maker SEB was the big winner from Soros's move, finishing up 2.89 percent at 1,032 francs.
"Seb is up because people feel it has better fundamentals (than Moulinex)," said one trader.
